r1-convention.title: Write down the evidence convention g1-implement.c1 depends on
r1-convention.imperative: The check you shipped requires payload status=complete on implementer-result evidence, and no document in this repo tells a Commander to attach it. Fix that at the source. Say it in the g1-implement imperative in skills/commander/templates/EXECUTE_PLAN.template.json itself (the template that carries the check must carry the instruction that satisfies it), and in skills/commander/references/commander-core.md and skills/commander/templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md. State the exact field name, that the value is the IMPLEMENTER_RESULT's own Return status, and that it is lowercase -- the engine's match is exact dict equality, so COMPLETE and COMPLETED both fail. Then pin it: tests/test_commander_evidence_convention.py, at least three tests, asserting the shipped template's check and the documented convention agree, and going red if either drifts.

postconditions.statement: the convention is documented and pinned by at least three passing tests

check.command: test $(python -m pytest -q tests/test_commander_evidence_convention.py --collect-only 2>/dev/null | grep -c '::') -ge 3 && env -u SPINE_FILE -u SPINE_SESSION -u SPINE_ENGINE NO_COLOR=1 python -m pytest -q tests/test_commander_evidence_convention.py

r2-satisfiable.title: Prove a Commander following the shipped instructions clears the gate
r2-satisfiable.imperative: Nobody has ever shown that a shipped template's gates can be satisfied by a real run -- that is why this defect shipped. Write tests/test_shipped_template_gates_satisfiable.py that instantiates EXECUTE_PLAN.template.json into a scratch work area, drives g1-implement through the real engine with evidence attached exactly as the imperative now instructs, and asserts it advances. Include the negative: evidence reporting the work blocked must refuse. Both directions, or it proves nothing.

r3-shipped-checks-run.title: Every shipped command check must actually run after instantiation
r3-shipped-checks-run.imperative: The cold reviewer found that REVIEW_SURVEY.template.json's r6-fowler.c1 ships a check command containing <fowler-pass-record-path>, a placeholder init_work_area.resolve_spine cannot resolve -- so the check is non-functional out of the box, and your census called that row 'already converted, no action'. Fix that placeholder, then sweep ALL six shipped role templates for the same shape: any command check whose text still holds an unresolved token after instantiation. Write tests/test_shipped_check_commands_resolve.py to pin it for every template, so a future author cannot ship another one. Report every site found, fixed or not.

why_trail.why: Documented the status=complete evidence convention (field name, Return-status source, lowercase rule) in EXECUTE_PLAN.template.json's g1-implement imperative, commander-core.md, and IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md; pinned it with 4 tests in tests/test_commander_evidence_convention.py that go red if the check's match dict or any of the three docs drift apart.

Wrote tests/test_shipped_template_gates_satisfiable.py: it instantiates EXECUTE_PLAN.template.json into a scratch dir, drives e0-context and g1-implement through the real checklist_engine.py CLI, attaches implementer-result evidence exactly as the new imperative documents (attach g1-implement --type implementer-result --field status=<value>), and asserts advance succeeds on status=complete and refuses (exit!=0, gate stays in-progress) on status=blocked. Both tests pass.

Swept the exact 6 templates named in checklist-engine.md's own Template set table for command checks holding an unresolved token after the real resolve_spine substitution. Found two phantom-placeholder sites of the same shape: REVIEW_SURVEY.template.json's r6-fowler.c1 (<fowler-pass-record-path>, the one the reviewer flagged) and INTERROGATION.template.json's zc-consolidate.c1 (<interrogation-record-path>, a second instance of the identical bug the sweep was written to catch). Both fixed by deriving the record path from <work-id> alone (.agent-work/<work-id>/FOWLER_PASS.json and .agent-work/<work-id>/INTERROGATION_RECORD.json), matching the already-established real convention and requiring no separate agent-invented substitution. Pinned with tests/test_shipped_check_commands_resolve.py: a closed allowlist for the one legitimate authoring-time placeholder shape (<exact test command>), zero tolerance for anything else, plus direct regression tests for both fixed sites.

Full suite reran clean (2542 passed, 1 skipped, 1102 subtests) and IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.md was written from the implementer template, including Workflow Feedback and an explicit accounting of what the first census missed (checked check-shape presence, never check-command resolvability) and that the new r3 sweep test would have caught it directly -- it did, finding a second unreported instance of the same bug in INTERROGATION.template.json.
